blockers.title: GNU build-ID equality does not authenticate that the executing kernel is the firmware-launched member
evidence: v31 makes currentExecution mandatory, but its only value is the NT_GNU_BUILD_ID note read from /sys/kernel/notes and compared with authenticatedKernelMember.gnuBuildId. The contract itself calls this value not a second authenticity digest and accepts any 64-hex-or-shorter note; it defines no content-digest algorithm, collision-resistance property, or uniqueness rule for the note.

A GNU build ID is an image label whose exact bytes can be chosen. A different kernel M can therefore be built with the same NT_GNU_BUILD_ID bytes as allowlisted K. Boot K through the measured firmware path, kexec M, and obtain the fresh TPM quote. PCR 0/1/2/4/7 still prove the firmware launch of K, while /sys/kernel/notes on honest M reports the copied build ID. Every new v31 equality passes although M is not authenticatedKernelMember.

The same observation is also supplied by the executing kernel being tested. A non-identical M controls the sysfs implementation and can expose K's note bytes without exposing K's executing bytes. No TPM measurement, immutable execution identity, or independently trusted current-image sensor joins currentExecution to the quote or to authenticatedKernelMember.sha256/peCoffImageDigest.

runtimeContinuity is explicitly optional hardening. After transition M may report kexec_loaded=0, and absent lockdown or kexec-disable indicators do not refuse. Thus those fields do not close the counterexample.

NT-TCB-KEXEC refuses only absent or unequal labels. It never tests the defining case in its own name when a different executing kernel carries the same label. PTCB-V30-B1 is therefore not repaired: the actual Linux host-ABI member can still be undeclared and drifted while the machine qualifies.
blockers.impact: A machine can satisfy the signed inventory, measured-boot transcript, fresh quote, package/member checks, and currentExecution equality while executing different kernel bytes. The required host-ABI TCB remains open and NT-TCB-1/NT-TCB-3/NT-TCB-KEXEC admit a false allow.
blockers.requiredRepair: Use an independently trusted, cryptographically content-bound observation of the currently executing kernel and compare it to the authenticated member, or enforce and attest an unbroken no-replacement interval from the measured launch through qualification. The current-image proof must be bound to this qualification event and fresh quote, fail closed when unavailable, and distinguish any different executing bytes even when build-ID note bytes are equal. NT_GNU_BUILD_ID may remain metadata but cannot be the sole pass/fail identity proof.

shouldFix.title: PCR-7 is inside the signed transcript in one rule and outside the live matcher and type-closure rules in others
evidence: measuredBootTranscript.covers and match require PCR-0/1/2/4/7 rows through the first separator on each PCR and explicitly put the PCR-7 SecureBoot/PK/KEK/db/dbx facts in the signed transcript.

The live measuredBootBind.measuredBootTranscriptMatch still requires only PCR-0/1/2/4 rows through the first PCR-4 separator. eventPreimage.unknownTypeRefuses and preKernelEventUnion.rule also remain limited to PCR-0/1/2/4. No roleGoverns or other precedence sentence selects the five-PCR rule.

The two intervals also differ for PCR 0/1/2: one ends at each PCR's own first separator, while the other ends at the first PCR-4 separator in global-log order. These are not equivalent in an interleaved event log.

A validator following the narrower live matcher can classify PCR-7 security facts from labels that were never equality-joined to the signed transcript; a validator following measuredBootTranscript.match must reject that same evidence. The claimed PTCB-V30-S6 repair is therefore only partially landed.
shouldFix.impact: Secure-Boot facts have inconsistent type-authentication standing, and conforming validators can disagree on the accepted transcript interval or use unauthenticated PCR-7 type labels.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define one governing transcript interval and one matcher for all selected PCRs. Propagate PCR 7 to measuredBootTranscriptMatch and to the closed type/classification rule, or define a separate closed PCR-7 config union and explicitly make it govern. Use the same per-PCR separator endpoints everywhere.

shouldFix.title: recomputeDigest still both requires and waives byte recomputation for the same code-bearing rows
evidence: recomputeDigest.rule normatively says that for each event the verifier constructs preimageBytes and recomputes the digest. PE_IMAGE_TYPES and BLOB_TYPES name exact image/blob bytes as those inputs.

preKernelReferences.join normatively says the opposite for every non-kernel code-bearing row whose bytes are not retained: signed digest equality replaces byte recomputation. No governing exception narrows the universal recomputeDigest.rule, and the row has no authenticated byte-source reference.

The ACTION branch says its retained input is trustedHandoff.callingFromBootOption.actionBytes, but the closed extras-rejected callingFromBootOption object has only action, globalLogIndex, pcr4SequenceIndex, preimageOk, pcrIndex, and eventType. actionBytes is not a lawful field. The exact eventLog is retained, but the named retained-location equality does not point to it.

v31 correctly removes eventPreimage(event) and fixes the TCG encodings, but it does not make one executable rule for when bytes are required and where those bytes come from. PTCB-V30-S3 is therefore only partially repaired.
shouldFix.impact: One implementation must refuse ordinary firmware code rows because required bytes are unavailable, while another may accept the same rows on signed digest equality alone. The ACTION proof also references a field the closed schema rejects.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make the byte-recomputation rule conditional and governing: enumerate the types/rows that must retain or resolve exact authenticated bytes, and explicitly exempt the rows for which signed digest equality is the intended proof. For every mandatory recomputation, name a lawful retained field or content-addressed authenticated source and join it to the event/transcript row. Point ACTION retention to an existing closed field or add actionBytes to that closed object.

advisories.title: Two residual references have no serializable target
evidence: kernelEventInclusion names callingFromBootOption and kernelEvent at their logIndex values, but both closed records define globalLogIndex and the kernel also defines pcr4SequenceIndex; neither defines logIndex.

tcgPfp permits a unique later revision the signed transcript names, while the closed transcript rows and signed digest carrier have no specification-revision field. Only the fixed Revision 1.06 v52 branch is currently serializable.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Replace logIndex with the intended retained index and either fix the PFP revision to 1.06 v52 or add one unambiguous signed revision selector outside the row list.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 1 blocker and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings.
conclusion: REJECT. v31 successfully adds a signed per-entry transcript digest and canonical join, makes runtimeContinuity consistently optional hardening, moves the remaining RPM extraction to roFd, repairs the TCG ACTION/VARIABLE encodings, and defines StartupLocality replay. It does not close NT-TCB-KEXEC: a different executing kernel can carry the same freely chosen GNU build-ID note and pass the only current-image equality while the quote continues to attest the firmware-launched kernel. PCR-7 transcript scope and byte-recomputation duties also remain internally inconsistent. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains in D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
